about: Spine and periphery theorems that stand apart from the base by design (U, 17 October 2026; the periphery of the run, the foundation and the inherited modules the bridge imports, since U2). Each root (an apart theorem no other apart theorem uses) has a category and a reason; THEOREM-CONNECTIVITY.py --check fails where an apart root has none. The categories: The F3 sweep (19 October 2026) removed the 218 entries whose modules left the run (superseded periphery modules, bridge and join modules); they are kept in the bridge-fold workspace, apart-retired.json.

categories.support: an arithmetic or list lemma, a statement using only the prelude, or a one-line unpacking of a module's own definitions
categories.logical-strength: a statement about LPO, WLPO, LLPO, excluded middle or choice only
categories.model-witness: a fact about one constructed model (a counterexample or example structure)
categories.restates: it restates a law already stated on the base
categories.general-structure: a law of every valuation or rule on any type; the base supplies no reading of its vocabulary
categories.bridge-interface: an equivalence between an inherited periphery interface and a core concept (the bridge ring)
categories.axiom-dependent: a periphery root whose own axiom report is not empty, so no join on the pure bridge can use it
categories.periphery-scope: a statement about a periphery module's own abstract interface with no evident reading as a process, run or world; the reason names the core concept the bridge identifies it with, or says there is none
categories.calibration: the exact logical principle (excluded middle, LPO, WLPO, choice) a stated criterion needs, for a notion the base does not assert; a lemma of the item that needs it
